title: Nutrient Regulation by Continuous Feeding for Large-scale Expansion of Mammalian Cells in Spheroids
protocol: Obtain β-TC6 cells or other desired adherent mammalian cell line.
Culture, passage, and cryopreserve the cells according to provider instructions.
Collect components needed for the feeding system: medium reservoir, peristaltic pump, stirred bioreactor, waste reservoir, tubing/sampling set.
Establish medium reservoir using a 1 L glass bottle.
Establish waste reservoir using a 2 L glass bottle.
Establish stirred bioreactor using a 250 ml volume glass reactor.
Use digital peristaltic pump or similar with an 8 channel pump head for medium exchange control.
Manufacture the reservoir and modified bioreactor lids from hard, autoclavable plastic.
Provide ventilation through sterile filters on the bioreactor lid.
Allow for medium transfer between reservoirs and bioreactors.
Optionally, include additional pass-through ports for instrumentation and monitoring probes.
Attach an outflow tube (OT) fabricated from porous glass aeration tubes with an average pore size range of 40 µm to 60 µm and a pore density of 40% to the modified SSB lid.
Assemble autoclavable perfusion tubing sets using polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) tubing connectors and durable peristaltic pump tubing.
Select two tubing diameters, L/S 14 for the primary tubing from the bioreactor to the medium reservoir, and L/S 13 for the pump section.
Insert a short length of L/S 13 tubing in the middle of the longer L/S 14 tubing using appropriate PVDF adaptors.
Join two pieces of L/S 14 tubing on either side of the shorter pump section (L/S 13) tubing using standard PVDF hose-barbed tubing adaptors.
Attach a sterile gas filter for gas venting to one clamped length.
Connect the second clamped length to a sterile sampling syringe.
Connect the third end to a stainless steel sample connector on the bioreactor lid.
Autoclave the entire sampling assembly while connected to the bioreactor.
Prepare all bioreactor components for autoclave sterilization.
Collect individual components for sterilization.
Sterilize medium and waste reservoirs (assembled from step 2.1.1).
Sterilize a 250 ml spinner flask (assembled from 2.1.1).
Sterilize necessary modified lids (assembled from 2.1.3).
Sterilize the outflow tube (described in 2.1.4).
Sterilize three tubing sets (assembled in sections 2.2 through 2.5).
Sterilize additional outflow tubes for continuous feeding.
Assemble spinner flask with all components and ensure outflow tube is firmly attached inside.
Attach the custom assembled sampling port to the top of the lid.
Wrap the spinner flask assembly with autoclave wrap material.
Attach autoclave indicating tape to ensure the seal is airtight.
Cover individual ends of each access port on the bioreactor lid with aluminum foil.
Assemble modified lids for medium and waste reservoirs and attach them to glass bottles.
Cover assembled lids using aluminum foil.
Wrap tubing sets individually with autoclave wrap material.
Seal individual ends of tubing sets with aluminum foil or similar material.
Autoclave all wrapped items using a standard dry cycle (Gravity setting, 15 psi, 121 °C for 30 min).
Perform all procedures post-autoclaving in a laminar flow hood.
Use sterile gloves to maintain sterile conditions during cell culture operations.
Culture β-TC6 cells in standard adherent cultures until sufficient quantities are obtained.
Assemble continuous feeding bioreactor with outflow tube as shown and described.
Connect sampling port to sampling lid of the bioreactor.
Sterilize modified SSB assembly by autoclaving.
Attach sterile vents (0.22 µm or smaller filters) to lids, medium, and waste vessels for gas exchange.
Collect cells by gentle trypsinization using 0.25% Trypsin-0.53 mM EDTA solution at room temperature with mechanical agitation.
Seed bioreactors with collected cells at a density of approximately 1.3 x 10^6 cells/ml in 200 ml culture medium.
Move designated flasks from the incubator into a Bio-Safety cabinet for cell culture and manipulations.
Remove culture medium from flasks by aspirating.
Wash cells with 5 ml of phosphate buffered saline without Ca++ or Mg++, rinse across the cells, and aspirate the PBS.
Add 3 ml of Trypsin-EDTA solution to each flask that will be collected.
Incubate harvested cells at room temperature for 2 - 3 min in a bio-safety cabinet.
Agitate gently by hand to loosen cells from flask surface.
Collect cells by adding 6 ml of culture medium with serum to the flask and transfer cells to a 50 ml tube.
Centrifuge collected cell suspensions at approximately 50 x gravity.
Aspirate remaining medium, leaving the pellet intact.
Re-suspend pellets in culture medium containing serum using a pipette.
Transfer all pellets into a single tube.
Count cell density using a standard hemocytometer with trypan blue staining.
Add desired number of total cells to sterile SSB for each condition.
Add medium with desired glucose concentration to SSB using a pipette to reach the total culture volume of 200 ml.
Move SSB with cells to a stir plate inside a cell culture incubator.
Culture cells in bioreactors without feeding for 3 days at 37 °C, with 5% CO2 and 100% relative humidity, at a stir rate of 70 rpm.
Autoclave or gas sterilize all components.
Assemble components in a biological safety cabinet using sterile techniques.
Remove the SSB from the incubator.
Assemble components for the continuous feeding system in a biological safety cabinet.
Fill the fresh medium reservoir with desired culture medium.
Connect one side of the feed line to the filled medium reservoir.
Install a sterile filter between the fresh medium reservoir and feed line.
Connect one side of the feed line to the feed inlet port on the bioreactor.
Install a sterile filter between the feed line and the bioreactor inlet port.
Connect the waste line to the bioreactor outflow tube.
Connect the other end of the waste line to the medium waste reservoir.
Ensure all connections are properly vented with sterile filters.
Move the assembly out of the biological safety cabinet.
Put all components out for long-term culture.
Place the SSB onto the stir plate inside the incubator using the same culture parameters for spheroid formation (37 °C, 5% CO2, 100% humidity and 70 rpm).
Temporarily disconnect tubing segments if necessary to run through holes in the side of the incubator.
Wrap ends of disconnected tubing sets with aluminum foil prior to autoclaving.
Attach bioreactor side of feed and waste tubes inside the incubator after removing foil.
Run remaining tubing sets out through the incubator access port or through a notch in the door gasket.
Connect the feed line to the fresh medium reservoir outside the incubator.
Connect the waste line to the medium waste reservoir outside the incubator.
Ensure the waste reservoir is properly vented with a sterile filter.
Place the fresh medium reservoir inside a nearby mini-refrigerator.
Check that the feed and waste lines can exit the incubator and enter the refrigerator without preventing door closure.
Verify that the feed lines are not pinched closed by the doors of either the refrigerator or the incubator.
Put the waste medium reservoir on the bench top outside the incubator.
Place the “pump section” of the feed and waste lines into the pump head ensuring proper orientation.
Turn the pump on to the desired feed rate.
Calculate the feed rate using the adjusted feed rate equation described in the literature and provided results section.
Use the most recent cell count information along with growth prediction and medium glucose measurements for estimation.
Set the pump speed based on the calculated feed rate.
Repeat the feed rate calculation and adjust the pump speed every three days.
Collect samples from each bioreactor every three days, or as desired.
Take culture samples from continuously fed SSB cultures using a specialized sampling port.
Attach a sterile syringe to the unfiltered connection of the sampling port.
Move the sampling tube down into the culture medium.
Unclamp the tube section going to the syringe.
Withdraw the desired total sample volume.
Move the sampling tube up out of the culture medium.
Continue to withdraw the syringe until air is removed.
Re-clamp the tube that feeds the syringe.
Detach the syringe containing the sample and set aside.
Attach a fresh sterile syringe pre-loaded with air to the sterile filter side of the sampling port.
Unclamp the tube going to the syringe-filter side of the sampling port.
Gently expel the air in the syringe through the sterile filter to purge the sampling port.
Re-clamp the tube going to the filter.
Disconnect and discard the sterile syringe used for purging.
Expel the cell sample from the syringe into a 10 ml tube.
Remove a known volume of cells for counting and transfer to a micro-centrifuge tube.
Gently centrifuge the micro-centrifuge tube for 1 - 2 min (approximately 50 x gravity).
Transfer the supernatant to a separate tube for glucose measurements.
Re-suspend the pellet with trypsin-EDTA solution (0.25% (w/v) trypsin, 0.53 mM EDTA).
Count cells in triplicate using a standard hemocytometer with trypan blue staining as described in the literature.
Add medium (with serum) to the sample for dilution as necessary.
Calculate cell viability by recording live and dead cells independently.
Measure medium glucose levels in triplicate using a blood glucose meter and single use test-strips.
Dip the test strip in the medium to be tested, collected from count samples above.
Test both fresh medium and waste medium for glucose concentrations.
After 3 days of culture, take 30 ml samples of the spheroid suspension and place in a 50 ml tube.
Gently pipette up and down using a wide diameter 25 ml pipette to distribute the suspension evenly.
Stop pipetting with the suspension at a known level in the pipet (e.g., 20 ml mark).
Record the time for all of the spheroids to settle 5 cm.
Repeat this procedure enough times to attain statistical confidence (usually n > 3).
